title: The workshop band on Wilson Avenue
summary: He gathers out-of-work players including Frank Teschemacher, Basil DuPre and Slim Evans to rehearse a band for fun in a dance studio.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs

blocks.x: And, then, so -- now, came we were doing really a workshop; I had a workshop band. I picked up all the guys in the neighborhood up on -- near Wilson Avenue,
All these guys were out of work and I said -- and I knew a guy that had a dance studio---
Wait a minute -- what part of Chicago---
North Side -- is that what they call the near North side--- or---

No -- it's the far North side-- Wilson Avenue is quite a ways up--- and, so, I was living out there and I got the best guys I could find that weren't doing anything, including Teshmacher--- and or the band --- I had Basil DuPre from the Isham Jones Band in that band and he doubled on trumpet; I had Teshmacher and---
Yeah and I had Slim Evans from the old days -- he was with the---
His name was Neirouter------ Otis Neirouter.

Yeah but they called him Slim Evans-- he got rid of that Neirouter thing-- and he was in Chicago so we got him and we had a guy - another saxophone player -- [Kensel C.] Toasty Paul who played alto, and first alto was Teshmacher and he played clarinet too and they all played clarinet - as a matter of fact. And, I had two -- [Mort] Croy was one of the trombones and I had a guy named Whitey [John] Whitehead-- Whitey Whitehead -- it was one of the trumpet players -- and, uh, I had another guy that had
been with Isham Jones Band and we formed this band -- for fun--- [Harold Moeller, second trumpet]
Yes and Don Carter was a great drummer at that time---
